domain_hypothesis.reasoning: The dataset contains columns such as 'InvoiceNo', 'StockCode', 'Description', 'Quantity', 'InvoiceDate', 'UnitPrice', 'CustomerID', and 'Country', which are classic schemas for online retail transaction logs (specifically matching the UCI Online Retail dataset).

kpi_specs.name: Total Revenue
kpi_specs.description: Calculates the total sales revenue generated across all transactions by multiplying Quantity and UnitPrice.
kpi_specs.sql_query: SELECT SUM(Quantity * UnitPrice) AS total_revenue FROM data
kpi_specs.reasoning: Total revenue is the primary financial metric for retail performance, best displayed as a single high-level summary card.

kpi_specs.name: Total Unique Customers
kpi_specs.description: Measures the distinct number of customers who have made purchases, excluding null customer profiles.
kpi_specs.sql_query: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT CustomerID) AS unique_customers FROM data WHERE CustomerID IS NOT NULL
kpi_specs.reasoning: Tracking the total active customer base is a fundamental growth metric, displayed cleanly on a summary card.

kpi_specs.name: Top 10 Countries by Revenue
kpi_specs.description: Identifies the top 10 countries generating the highest total sales revenue.
kpi_specs.sql_query: SELECT Country, SUM(Quantity * UnitPrice) AS total_revenue FROM data GROUP BY Country ORDER BY total_revenue DESC LIMIT 10
kpi_specs.reasoning: A bar chart is ideal for comparing sales performance across geographical regions, helping identify key market segments.

kpi_specs.name: Top 10 Best Selling Products by Quantity
kpi_specs.description: Lists the top 10 products based on the total physical quantity sold.
kpi_specs.sql_query: SELECT Description, SUM(Quantity) AS total_quantity FROM data WHERE Description IS NOT NULL GROUP BY Description ORDER BY total_quantity DESC LIMIT 10
kpi_specs.reasoning: Visualizing product demand via a bar chart helps inventory managers quickly spot high-velocity inventory items.

kpi_specs.name: Chronological Sales Trend
kpi_specs.description: Shows the chronological progression of sales amounts over time based on the invoice transaction timestamps.
kpi_specs.sql_query: SELECT substr(InvoiceDate, 1, 10) AS InvoiceDate, SUM(Quantity * UnitPrice) AS sales_amount FROM data GROUP BY substr(InvoiceDate, 1, 10) ORDER BY InvoiceDate ASC
kpi_specs.reasoning: A line chart over sequential InvoiceDate timestamps captures transactional sales momentum without relying on non-standard SQL date functions.
